root_shape.rule_skill_loop: The system owner writes one rule for an agent — and the rule can be as complex as he wants — and that rule is fixed: no tool ever writes it. Everything else is generated around it. An AI agent then writes the fix text, clear instructions for Claude Code on how the agent could be repaired in 3 minutes or less if it breaks; next come the RED definition, the exact machine-checkable conditions for what "broken" means, and the GREEN definition, the same for what "healthy" means — both dynamically generated and real. A second, blind AI pass then validates that the fix matches the goal and that the RED, the GREEN, and the fix all genuinely satisfy the owner's rule, rating the whole thing LEGIT or STUPID with its reasoning recorded. Separately, the agent has self-healing through an index of exactly 10 skills extracted from a knowledge store — searched with ripgrep for fast lookup — and converted into plain-English instructions, each carrying its own RED or GREEN status from a blind AI review and tested as the system grows and evolves; a RED skill is quarantined — kept in its slot but excluded from fix prompts — until a better one reviews GREEN, and a GREEN skill is replaced only by something better. When the agent breaks, all the information — minus the RED skills — is passed to Claude Code to fix, and the red only clears when the agent's own check reports GREEN; SSE live streaming pushes the red alert to the screen and shows the agent fixing it in real time. After the fix, the knowledge base is updated with the lesson, the skills and rule parts are regenerated against it, and the agent gets stronger and faster over time. That is the positive feedback: every break deposits a lesson, every lesson feeds the next generation, and the system continuously improves. It's like a two-headed cat where one head looks back at what was learned and one head looks forward at what's coming, both at the same time.
